text:
The Oilers are 11-3-3 with 25 points and 70 goals, the kind of total that makes a 17-game sample look like a juggernaut. Our numbers are less sure. Edmonton has scored 18.5 goals more than its chances would predict, a gap that almost never holds over a season, and our model counts about five points of luck in the standings. Even at five on five, they're getting 49% of the expected goals.

Some of that finishing is real, because some of it is Connor McDavid and Leon Draisaitl. With Vasily Podkolzin on their wing, the top line has outscored opponents 17-6 at five on five on 62% of the chances in 198 minutes. Mattias Ekholm and Evan Bouchard have been on for 17 goals and allowed four.

The rest is the problem. The Mathieu Joseph, Alex Formenton and Owen Michaels line has 35% of the expected goals and has been outscored 9-5. Connor Murphy and Ryan Shea have logged the most minutes of any pair (227) at 45% of the chances and 40% of the shot attempts. When the shooting cools, those minutes are where it will show.

The odds still love them: 95% to make the playoffs, a 104-point pace, a coin flip for the Pacific. The question for the next month is whether the depth can tread water once the goals stop arriving at this rate.
headline: Edmonton's shooters are writing cheques the chances can't cash
